Elaine — appreciate the clarity. Drafting a compact playbook to cover the options you asked for. High level below; attaching a cost model and a tracked SOW.

Key proposals (summary):
1) Term and co-terming: 36-month master term aligned to July 1 start (co-term). Quarterly reconciliation windows at Q1/Q2/Q3 to allow staged ramp.

2) Staggered ramp schedule (year 1):
   - Q1: 20% committed capacity (baseline)
   - Q2: 40% (onboard + initial growth)
   - Q4: 100% (full commit)
   - True-up: at each quarter-end; small overage billing until true-up settles

3) Auto-renew: auto-renew enabled by default. Opt-out window: 60 days before renewal date. For multi-year, opt-out applies to the annual renewal slice.

4) Clawback / credits: pro-rated credits applied to future invoices for under-utilization in year 1 only. Applies only if shortfall >15% against committed tokens; excludes burst capacity and Marketplace usage.

5) Surge / emergency path: On-demand burst pool (metered) + canary fallback model for high-latency situations. Guaranteed hold-back capacity for first 30 days after major scale events.

Next steps: if this aligns, we (Karthik) will produce redlines for the SOW and contract language for the clawback and opt-out windows.

Attaching: Orbit_SOW_v2.pdf, redwood_cost_model_v3.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Renewal Strategy, Redwood Inference

- Recommend tightening the auto-renew opt-out to 45 days (we can be more flexible operationally, and it looks better to finance).
- Suggest a two-tier clawback: 15-30% shortfall => credits only; >30% shortfall => credits + one-time onboarding discount on next quarter. That gives Orbit a safety net without unlocking refunds.
- Add a billing cadence option: quarterly invoices (default) or annual prepay with a 4% discount.

Elaine / team — looping in contract language per Camila's note. Below are the proposed snippets you can drop into the SOW / MSA (cleaner text follows in Doc):

- Opt-Out: "Customer may elect to not renew any upcoming annual renewal slice by providing written notice to Redwood no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the renewal date."

- Clawback / Credits: "If Customer's realized usage for any quarterly reconciliation period is less than eighty-five percent (85%) of the Customer's committed capacity for that period, Redwood will issue a pro-rated credit equal to the unused committed portion, applied to subsequent invoices. If shortfall exceeds thirty percent (30%) for a given reconciliation period, Redwood will additionally apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the quarterly committed fee to the following quarter's invoice (not payable in cash)."

- True-up Timing: "Quarterly reconciliation will occur within 30 days of quarter-end; adjustments reflected on the following invoice."

Camila — I left the opt-out at 45 days per your recommendation. Elaine — confirm if 45 days works for Orbit; if not, we can move back to 60.

Karthik
